mainTopic: Whether difficult use counts as use (the pit and the shallow pool), רב יהודה on flipping a bundle of reeds, and the threshold as a מקום פטור
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about a person who sets his שבת place in רשות הרבים and puts his עירוב in a pit. 'Above ten טפחים' the עירוב works, and 'below ten' it fails. The גמרא shows this must mean a shallow pit. That seems to prove that תשמיש על ידי הדחק שמיה תשמיש, against רבא. רבא gives two answers. In the first, both the person and the pit are a כרמלית. In the second, the food is in a כרמלית and the ברייתא follows רבי, who holds that a שבות was not decreed during בין השמשות. רבא then proves his rule from the doubled wording in the משנה of a shallow pool (רקק מים): walking with difficulty counts as walking, but use with difficulty does not count as use. Next, רב יהודה rules that flipping a bundle of reeds along the ground creates no liability until it is lifted. The גמרא then returns to the ברייתא of a person standing on a threshold. After rejecting רשות הרבים, רשות היחיד and כרמלית, it concludes the threshold is a מקום פטור smaller than four by four טפחים, supported by רבי יוחנן. Finally, the ruling that passing an object across through the threshold leaves all three פטור is raised as a challenge to רבא, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: An עירוב Placed in a Pit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if someone set his שבת place in רשות הרבים and put his עירוב in a pit, it works 'above ten טפחים' and fails 'below ten טפחים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone intended to rest on שבת in רשות הרבים, and he put his עירוב in a pit above ten טפחים, his עירוב is valid. If he put it below ten טפחים, his עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that will soon be used to challenge the view that awkward use does not count as use. Right now it is only laying out the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין works only if the person could reach his food at the start of שבת without breaking שבת. If the food sits in a different רשות than he does, he cannot bring it out, and the עירוב fails. The ברייתא says the pit's depth decides whether the food counts as being in the same place as the person.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended to set his שבת resting place
Here, עירוב תחומין: food placed to set a person's שבת 'home base'
The public domain
A pit
Handbreadths, about 8-10 cm each

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole sugya depends on what case this ברייתא is describing. The גמרא's reading of it becomes the basis for the challenge.

phrases.english: If he intended to establish his Shabbat place in the public domain,
and he placed his eiruv in a pit
above ten handbreadths —
phrases.notes: The גמרא will soon ask what exactly this means.

phrases.english: his eiruv is a valid eiruv.
Below ten handbreadths —
his eiruv is not a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Source text brought to test the earlier claim about תשמיש על ידי הדחק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב in a pit 'above ten' is valid; 'below ten' is invalid, for one who set his place in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: What Case Is This? First Suggestion: A Deep Pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. It first suggests a pit ten טפחים deep, where 'above' and 'below' mean the food was raised up or pushed down inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is a pit that is ten טפחים deep, and 'above' means he raised the עירוב up and placed it there, and 'below' means he lowered it and placed it there...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind the ברייתא and offers a first possible reading. This sets up the next step, which will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal is one deep pit, with 'above ten' and 'below ten' referring to where inside the pit the food was placed. This is the most obvious reading, so the גמרא tests it first.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
That he raised it up and placed it
That he lowered it and placed it

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say it is a pit that has ten handbreadths of depth,
and 'above' means that he raised it and placed it there,
phrases.notes: He put the food on a raised spot inside the pit, within ten טפחים of ground level.

phrases.english: and 'below' means that he lowered it and placed it there,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּבוֹר דְּאִית בֵּיהּ עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the ברייתא in step 1 describes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What physical setup does the ברייתא mean by 'above ten' and 'below ten'?

steps.title: Rejecting the Deep Pit Reading
steps.stepSummary: In a pit ten טפחים deep, it makes no difference where the food is placed. The whole pit is a רשות היחיד, so the person and his עירוב are always in different domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make to me if it is above, and what difference if it is below? Either way, he is in one place and his עירוב is in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. In a deep pit, 'above' and 'below' would make no difference at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit ten טפחים deep is a רשות היחיד from its floor all the way up. Raising the food inside it does not move the food into רשות הרבים. So the person, who is in רשות הרבים, could never take his food, and the ברייתא's distinction would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me?
In a different place (a different רשות)

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי לְמַעְלָה וּמָה לִי לְמַטָּה.
phrases.english: What difference is it to me whether above or below?
He is in one place (the public domain),
and his eiruv is in another place (the private domain).

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִי לְמַעְלָה וּמָה לִי לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the reading proposed in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as one pit ten טפחים deep
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A deep pit is entirely a רשות היחיד, so the food's height inside it changes nothing.

steps.title: So It Must Be a Shallow Pit, Which Proves Awkward Use Counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean a pit less than ten טפחים deep, and it says the עירוב works. That implies תשמיש על ידי הדחק שמיה תשמיש, which challenges רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not a pit that does not have ten טפחים of depth, and it teaches that his עירוב is valid? This shows that use under difficulty is considered use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the only reading left: a shallow pit. From that reading it draws a conclusion that contradicts רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Above ten' means a shallow pit, under ten טפחים deep, and 'below ten' means a deep one. The עירוב in the shallow pit works, so the person and his food must be in the same domain, רשות הרבים. A shallow pit can count as part of רשות הרבים only if using it, even awkwardly, counts as real use, and that contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (introduces the forced reading)
And it teaches
Evidently / this proves
Use that is done with difficulty or awkwardness
Is called (counts as) use

steps.confusionAlert: In this reading, 'above ten' and 'below ten' do not describe positions inside one pit. They describe two different pits: a shallow one (bottom above ten טפחים) and a deep one (bottom below ten טפחים).
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether awkward use counts as use decides whether things like shallow pits belong to רשות הרבים. That changes the law of carrying and of עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּבוֹר דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not about a pit that does not have ten handbreadths of depth,
and it teaches that his eiruv is a valid eiruv?
Evidently, use under difficulty
is considered use.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּבוֹר דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the deep-pit reading, adopts the shallow-pit reading and draws a conclusion from it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עירוב in a shallow pit works only if the pit is part of רשות הרבים. That is true only if awkward use counts as use.

steps.title: רבא's Answer: Both Were in a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the person and his עירוב were both in a כרמלית. The ברייתא says 'רשות הרבים' only to mean 'not a רשות היחיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he would answer him: he and his עירוב are in a כרמלית. And why does it call it 'רשות הרבים'? Because it is not a רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his view by reading the ברייתא differently. The person set his place in a כרמלית, and the shallow pit is also a כרמלית, so both are in the same domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person is in a כרמלית, the shallow pit can also be a כרמלית without needing awkward use to count as use. Then he and his food are in one domain and the עירוב works. The ברייתא's word 'רשות הרבים' is read loosely, as any area that is not a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: At times he would answer him (one of several answers given)
An in-between domain, neither fully public nor private, restricted only by the רבנן
And why does it call it...?
The private domain

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא seems to prove that awkward use counts as use. רבא avoids that proof by placing the case in a כרמלית and reading 'רשות הרבים' as 'not a רשות היחיד'.

phrases.english: At times he would answer him:
phrases.notes: 'At times' signals that רבא gave more than one answer. This is the first.

phrases.english: he and his eiruv are in a karmelit,
and why does it call it 'public domain'? —
because it is not the private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִמְנִין מְשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ הוּא וְעֵירוּבוֹ בְּכַרְמְלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case: the location is a כרמלית, and the ברייתא's term is read loosely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'רשות הרבים' means a true public domain, so a shallow pit must count as public through awkward use.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the person and the shallow pit are a כרמלית, so they are one domain without needing to say awkward use counts as use.

steps.title: A second answer: person in a public domain, food in a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רבא sometimes answered differently. The person really was in רשות הרבים and his עירוב was in a כרמלית (the shallow pit). The ברייתא follows רבי, who says rabbinic prohibitions were not decreed during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And sometimes he would answer him: the person was in רשות הרבים and his עירוב was in a כרמלית. And this ברייתא follows רבי, who said that anything forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree (שבות) was not decreed during בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same challenge from Step 4. This time he takes the words 'רשות הרבים' literally and puts only the food in a כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit less than ten טפחים deep is a כרמלית, not part of רשות הרבים. Carrying from a כרמלית to רשות הרבים is only a rabbinic prohibition (שבות). רבי holds the rabbis did not apply their decrees during בין השמשות, which is the moment an עירוב takes effect. So the person could reach his food at that moment, and the עירוב works without saying that difficult use counts as use.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes he would answer him (an alternative answer)
An in-between domain, neither fully public nor private; its rules are rabbinic
A rabbinic שבת prohibition, not a Torah one
Twilight, the moment when an עירוב takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this answer with Step 5. There, both the person and the food were in a כרמלית. Here, the person really is in רשות הרבים and only the food is in the כרמלית.

phrases.english: And sometimes he would answer him:
he was in the public domain
and his eiruv was in a karmelit.
phrases.notes: A pit less than ten טפחים deep is a כרמלית.

phrases.english: And it is the view of Rebbi, who said:
anything that is forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree,
they did not decree it during twilight.
phrases.notes: An עירוב takes effect at twilight, so the food was reachable at that moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative answer to the same challenge that Step 5 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (food in a כרמלית) and attributes the ברייתא to רבי's view on שבות during בין השמשות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's ruling that the עירוב works shows that difficult use counts as use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב works because carrying from a כרמלית is only a שבות, which רבי does not apply during בין השמשות. Difficult use is not involved.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the משנה of a shallow pool
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he is not just deflecting the question; he means his answers precisely. He quotes a משנה about a shallow pool (less than ten טפחים) that רשות הרבים passes through. Someone who throws four אמות into it is liable. The משנה seems to say this twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say I am just pushing you off; I am saying it precisely. As we learned in a משנה: if there was a shallow pool of water and רשות הרבים passes through it, one who throws four אמות into it is liable. And how deep is a shallow pool? Less than ten טפחים. And a shallow pool that רשות הרבים passes through, one who throws four אמות into it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his position by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the actual proof comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the משנה seems to repeat itself: both 'רקק' and 'רשות הרבים passes through it' appear twice. The גמרא will use these repetitions to prove that difficult use is not considered use.

keyTerms.meaning: I am just pushing you off (with a weak answer)
Precisely, meant exactly
A shallow pool or puddle of water
Walks through it, passes through it
One who throws

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's rule is not just a way to escape a question. He has a source for it in a משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא תֵּימָא דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵינָא לָךְ,
phrases.english: And do not say that I am just pushing you off;
rather, I am telling you something precise.
As we learned in a mishna: If there was a shallow pool of water
and the public domain passes through it,
one who throws four cubits within it is liable.
And how deep is a shallow pool?
Less than ten handbreadths.

phrases.aramaic: וּרְקָק מַיִם שֶׁרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְהַלֶּכֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: And a shallow pool that the public domain passes through,
phrases.notes: This is the line that seems to repeat something already said.

phrases.english: one who throws four cubits within it is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תֵּימָא דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵינָא לָךְ, אֶלָּא דַּוְקָא קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ. דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answers by bringing a source for his rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רקק מים through which רשות הרבים passes

steps.title: Why the word רקק appears twice: summer and rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first repetition. One mention of 'רקק' covers summer and the other covers the rainy season. Both are needed, because each season has its own reason people might enter the pool.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable why 'רקק' is said twice: one is for summer and one is for the rainy season. Both are needed. Had it taught only summer, I would think that applies because people go in to cool off, but in the rainy season it does not. Had it taught only the rainy season, I would think that applies because people are already muddy and walk right in, but in summer it does not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accounts for the first repetition in the משנה, the word 'רקק'. This sets up the next step, which asks about the repetition that is still unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In summer, people walk through the pool to cool off. In the rainy season, they are already dirty, so they don't avoid it. Each reason applies to only one season, so the משנה must mention both. This explains one repetition, but not the double 'passes through'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (introduces something that is fine, before raising a difficulty)
It is necessary (both cases are needed)
The summer days
The rainy season
He is dirty or muddy

phrases.english: Granted, 'pool' 'pool' is said twice:
one for the summer
and one for the rainy season.
And both are necessary,
for had it taught us only about the summer,
I would say that is because people commonly go in to cool themselves,
but in the rainy season, I would say not.
And had it taught us only about the rainy season,
I would say that is because, since he is already muddy, he goes right in,
but in the summer, not.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first repetition in the משנה quoted in Step 7, to set up the question about the second one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה mention 'רקק' twice?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention is for summer and one is for the rainy season. Each is needed because each has a different reason.

steps.title: Walking with difficulty counts; using with difficulty does not
steps.stepSummary: Why does the משנה say twice that רשות הרבים passes through the pool? To teach that walking with difficulty counts as walking, but difficult use does not count as use. The גמרא concludes: שמע מינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need 'passes through' twice? Must we not learn from this that walking with difficulty is considered walking, but use with difficulty is not considered use? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the extra 'passes through' in the משנה and draws רבא's rule from it. It then concludes that the proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking through a shallow pool is hard, yet the משנה treats the pool as part of רשות הרבים. So walking with difficulty counts as walking. The משנה stresses that people actually walk through the pool, meaning that awkward use of it alone would not be enough. So difficult use is not considered use, exactly as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking, passing through
With difficulty, under strain
Why do I need it?
Must we not learn from this?
Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Walking with difficulty counts as walking (הילוך על ידי הדחק שמיה הילוך). Use with difficulty does not count as use (תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש). This is how רבא's rule is proven from the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'difficult' means 'doesn't count' across the board. The גמרא splits the two: walking with difficulty counts, but using with difficulty does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms רבא's rule against the challenge from the ברייתא of the pit. His answers in Steps 5 and 6 were real explanations, not just escapes.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הִילּוּךְ תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: But why do I need 'passes through' twice?
Rather, must we not learn from this

phrases.aramaic: הִילּוּךְ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק — שְׁמֵיהּ הִילּוּךְ,
phrases.english: that walking with difficulty is considered walking,

phrases.aramaic: תַּשְׁמִישׁ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק — לָא שְׁמֵיהּ תַּשְׁמִישׁ.
phrases.english: but use with difficulty is not considered use?
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הִילּוּךְ תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained the repeated 'רקק', the גמרא uses the still-unexplained repetition of 'passes through' to finish רבא's proof.
steps.raayaObject: תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double mention of 'רשות הרבים מהלכת בו' in the משנה of רקק מים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Walking with difficulty counts as walking, but difficult use is not considered use. This supports רבא.

steps.title: Flipping a bundle of reeds without lifting it
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person who flips a bundle of reeds end over end along the ground is not liable until he lifts it completely off the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Someone takes a bundle of reeds, tips it down and stands it up, tips it down and stands it up again, moving it along this way. He is not liable until he actually lifts it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling about moving an object without ever really lifting it. Even if the bundle travels a long way, there is no liability yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be liable for carrying on שבת, a person must do an עקירה (lift the object from its place) and a הנחה (set it down). When the bundle is flipped end over end, one end always stays on the ground, so it was never truly lifted. That means no עקירה happened, and he is not liable no matter how far the bundle moves.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle
Reeds
He tipped it down and stood it up (flipping it end over end)
He lifted it up from its place (the act of עקירה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Torah prohibition of carrying depends on the specific act of lifting and setting down, not just on the object ending up in a different place.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is not liable because the distance is short. Distance is not the issue. The issue is that the object was never fully lifted off the ground.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This bundle of reeds,
he tipped it down and stood it up
tipped it down and stood it up again
phrases.notes: He keeps flipping it end over end, so one end always touches the ground.

phrases.english: he is not liable
until he lifts it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַאי זִירְזָא דְּקָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a related side ruling. Like the earlier discussion of moving things in unusual ways, it deals with when moving an object counts as a real act of carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flipping a bundle end over end along the ground is not liable until a full עקירה (lifting) takes place.

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא about the threshold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא: a person on a threshold may take from and give to both the homeowner and the poor man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A person stands on the threshold. He may take from the homeowner and give to him. He may also take from the poor man and give to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote a line from the earlier ברייתא about the domains of שבת. It is setting up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The homeowner stands inside in רשות היחיד, and the poor man stands outside in רשות הרבים. The ברייתא allows the person on the threshold to pass objects both ways. That only makes sense if the threshold itself is neither of those two domains.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said" (a formula for quoting a ברייתא or earlier teaching that is about to be discussed)
Threshold or doorstep
The homeowner (standing inside the house)
A poor man (standing outside in the street)

phrases.english: The Master said:
A person standing on the threshold
may take from the homeowner and give to him,
may take from the poor man and give to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל הָאִסְקוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יהודה's side ruling, the גמרא returns to the main ברייתא about the four domains of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person on a threshold may pass objects to and from both the house and the street.

steps.title: What kind of threshold is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what type of threshold the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of threshold the ברייתא means. This question sets up the next steps: steps 13-15 test and reject three possible answers, and step 16 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different thresholds can have different halachic status. Depending on its height, size and position, a threshold can be רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים, a כרמלית, or a מקום פטור. The גמרא needs to know which one the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: "This ... what is it?" (a request to define the case)

phrases.english: This threshold, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the exact case behind the ברייתא quoted in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the halachic status of the threshold in the ברייתא?

steps.title: It cannot be a public-domain threshold
steps.stepSummary: If the threshold is רשות הרבים, he could not take from the homeowner, because that would be carrying out from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a threshold that counts as רשות הרבים, how can he take from the homeowner? He would be carrying out from רשות היחיד into רשות הרבים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible answer and shows that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the threshold were רשות הרבים, taking from the homeowner inside would mean moving an object from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים. That is forbidden carrying, yet the ברייתא allows it. So this option does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say" (introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected)
Public domain
Private domain
He is carrying out

phrases.english: If you say it is a threshold that is public domain,
how can he take from the homeowner?

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַפֵּיק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים!
phrases.english: He is carrying out from the private domain to the public domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests the first possible answer to the question in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the threshold is רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking from the homeowner would then be carrying from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים, which contradicts the ברייתא's permission.

steps.title: It cannot be a private-domain threshold either
steps.stepSummary: If the threshold is רשות היחיד, he could not take from the poor man, because that would be carrying in from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is a threshold that counts as רשות היחיד. Then how can he take from the poor man? He would be carrying in from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second possible answer, and it fails too. This sets up the need for a different explanation, which steps 15-16 go on to supply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the threshold were רשות היחיד, taking from the poor man outside would mean moving an object from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד. That is also forbidden. Since neither option works, the גמרא must try another kind of threshold. The next step tests a כרמלית, and only after that fails does the גמרא settle on a מקום פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather" (moves on to the next option after the first one failed)
He is carrying in
An exempt area that is neither private nor public domain (the likely direction of the answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lets objects pass both ways across the threshold. Calling it רשות הרבים breaks the "from the homeowner" case, and calling it רשות היחיד breaks the "from the poor man" case. The גמרא now has to find another kind of threshold.

phrases.english: Rather, say it is a threshold that is private domain,
how can he take from the poor man?

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מְעַיֵּיל מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד!
phrases.english: He is carrying in from the public domain to the private domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option failed in step 13, this tests the second option and shows that it fails too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the threshold is רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking from the poor man would then be carrying from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד, which also contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: A כרמלית threshold does not work either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to say the threshold is a כרמלית. It rejects this because a כרמלית is still rabbinically forbidden, yet the ברייתא allows taking and giving from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is a threshold that is a כרמלית. But the ברייתא says he may take and give from the start. In the end, there is still a prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: After ruling out רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד, the גמרא tries a third option, that the threshold is a כרמלית. It immediately knocks this down as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying between a כרמלית and another domain is not a Torah violation, but the חכמים forbade it. The ברייתא uses the word for permission from the start, which means no prohibition at all. So a כרמלית cannot be what the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between area that is neither a true public nor a true private domain. Carrying there is forbidden מדרבנן.
From the start, fully permitted
In the end, after all
At least a prohibition exists

steps.confusionAlert: פטור is not the same as מותר. A כרמלית makes you exempt from a Torah penalty, but it is still forbidden. The ברייתא's word לכתחלה demands that the act be truly permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, a threshold that is a karmelit
phrases.notes: This is the third try at explaining what kind of threshold is meant.

phrases.english: [yet the baraita says] he takes and gives from the start?
In the end, there is at least a prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects a third possibility after steps 13 and 14 ruled out the first two.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the threshold as a כרמלית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כרמלית is rabbinically forbidden, but the ברייתא allows the act לכתחלה.

steps.title: The threshold is an exempt area smaller than four by four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the threshold is a מקום פטור, meaning it is smaller than four by four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the threshold is simply an exempt area, for example where it is not four טפחים by four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the threshold is a מקום פטור. That is an area too small to count as any domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An area smaller than four by four טפחים does not count as a domain for שבת at all. So taking from it or placing onto it is not carrying between domains, and there is no prohibition. This fits the ברייתא's permission לכתחלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An exempt area that belongs to no domain
Merely, simply
Four by four טפחים, the minimum size of a domain
That does not have in it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next steps. If the threshold is a מקום פטור, then passing an object through it raises the question of whether the transfer counts as direct carrying.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִסְקוּפָּה מְקוֹם פָּטוּר בְּעָלְמָא הוּא —
phrases.english: Rather, the threshold is merely an exempt place

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.english: for example, where it does not have four by four [handbreadths]

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִסְקוּפָּה מְקוֹם פָּטוּר בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 12 after three options failed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The threshold had to be one of the standard domains, and each one led to a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The threshold is a מקום פטור, smaller than four by four טפחים, so the ברייתא's permission works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The threshold is a מקום פטור: an area smaller than four by four טפחים, which belongs to no domain. So taking from it and giving onto it is permitted לכתחלה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's parallel ruling about small exempt areas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its answer with רבי יוחנן's ruling, brought by רב דימי. People from both domains may use a small exempt area, as long as they do not exchange objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב דימי said in the name of רבי יוחנן when he came from ארץ ישראל: A place that is not four by four טפחים may be used by people of רשות היחיד and people of רשות הרבים to rest their loads on, as long as they do not exchange with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer by citing a known ruling of רבי יוחנן about small exempt areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that people of both domains may use an area smaller than four by four טפחים freely. This matches the ברייתא's permission. He adds one limit: they may not swap objects across the domains through it. That limit sets up the next quote from the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came [from ארץ ישראל to בבל]
To adjust or rest a load on the shoulder
As long as they do not exchange
Handbreadths

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
phrases.english: And it is like that which, when Rav Dimi came,
[he said that] Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים —
phrases.english: A place that does not have four by four handbreadths
is permitted for the people of the private domain
and for the people of the public domain to rest their loads on it,
as long as they do not exchange [objects].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ruling to support the מקום פטור answer of step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The definition of the threshold as a מקום פטור that may be used from both sides
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling as reported by רב דימי

steps.title: The ברייתא's limit: do not pass between homeowner and poor man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the ברייתא. One may not take from the homeowner and give to the poor man, or the reverse. But if he did, all three are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: As long as he does not take from the homeowner and give to the poor man, or take from the poor man and give to the homeowner. And if he took and gave, all three are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבי יוחנן's limit of not exchanging. Passing an object across through the threshold is forbidden. Even so, the ברייתא says no one is liable: not the homeowner, not the poor man, and not the person on the threshold. The object went through a מקום פטור and was not carried directly from one domain to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said, a formula for quoting an earlier source
The homeowner, standing in רשות היחיד
The poor man, standing in רשות הרבים
All three are exempt

phrases.english: The Master said:
as long as he does not take from the homeowner
and give to the poor man,
[or take] from the poor man and give to the homeowner.
And if he took and gave,
all three of them are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִטּוֹל מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 11 to quote its next clause, which will be the basis of a new challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing an object between רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים through a מקום פטור is forbidden, but no one is liable.

steps.title: Does the baraita refute רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא's exemption contradicts רבא, who holds that carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים creates liability even when the object travels overhead. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבא? For רבא said: One who moves an object from the beginning of four אמות to the end of four אמות in רשות הרבים, even though he moved it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רבא based on the ברייתא's ruling that all three are פטור. It begins quoting רבא's rule, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that moving an object four אמות in רשות הרבים makes a person liable even if it passes above the ten-טפחים height of רשות הרבים. That airspace is a מקום פטור, so passing through a מקום פטור does not break the transfer. By the same logic, passing an object from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים through the threshold, which is also a מקום פטור, should create liability. Yet the ברייתא says all three are פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say
A conclusive refutation
One who moves or transfers
Four cubits, the distance for liability in רשות הרבים

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's statement is cut off here. The full point, that he is liable even though the object passed above him, appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rava?
For Rava said:
One who transfers an object
from the beginning of four [cubits] to the end of four
in the public domain,
even though he transferred it
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of step 18 that all three are פטור to challenge רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule about transferring an object four אמות in רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבא's case the object passes through a מקום פטור (above ten טפחים) and he is still liable. So an object passing from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים through the threshold, also a מקום פטור, should create liability. The ברייתא says everyone is פטור.
